prompt:
Desktop web application UI comp at 1536 by 1024, not a poster and not a photograph. Product: Infrastructure AI Agent, an operations workspace for multiple bridge inspection runs. Direction: Corridor Command Map, drawing from transport control maps, work-zone boards, route diagrams, and precise engineering interfaces. Restrained palette only: mist gray #E8ECE8 page, near-black green #18231F text, route teal #176B62, work-zone amber #E1B13D, white working surfaces. No gradients, no glass, no decorative imagery, no sample images, no huge headline, no floating card grid.

Composition C: compact full-width header with product mark and three system indicators. Beneath, a 240px run ledger sits at left with filters, active/completed/failed counts, and dense rows. The center is a broad selected-run workspace. Its top third is a corridor timeline: a thin route starts at media upload and passes through Evidence, Severity, Retrieval, Planning, Scheduling, and Report; each node owns a concise real status line and elapsed time. Below the route, a bold but compact selected case title and six result tabs. The active Observations tab displays a structured evidence table with source thumbnail placeholders, defect, location, confidence, severity hint, and trace ID. A fixed 320px right inspector pane shows run summary, current worker heartbeat, retries, review state, and actions to export or approve. A slide-over New Inspection panel is partially open from the right edge, proving intake can happen without losing the selected run. Use precise alignment, thin directional lines, crisp dividers, almost no shadows, compact sans typography, tabular numbers, 4-6px corners, and clear keyboard focus.

The interface should feel like transport operations software redesigned for evidence-driven bridge maintenance: distinctive through topology, not decoration.
